title: Normalized Weil open unit and the empty geometric fibre
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $j_0:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be an open immersion of finite-type $k_0$-schemes (not assumed separated) and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its base change [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. The scheme and algebraically closed coefficient universes are independent; finite coefficient fields use their canonical small models. Use the constructible coefficient categories and Weil pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], $G_T=Lg_T^*$ and restriction $j^*=Lj^*$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $J=Rj_!$ for the compact-support operation of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] with compactification $(j,\operatorname{id}_X)$ and its specified coefficient action [def-weil-compact-support-coefficient-action].

At $\Lambda=E$ for every finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$, and at $\Lambda=\Qlb$, let $\alpha:G_Uj^*\simeq j^*G_X$ be the pullback-composition comparison. There is a canonical comparison $\beta:G_XJ\simeq JG_U$: its integral version is the completed open base-change comparison for the square along $g_X$, transported through the comparison of ordinary integral and completed pullback. With the open adjunction $J\dashv j^*$, whose unit is $\eta:\operatorname{id}\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*J$, this comparison satisfies the actual normalized equation
$$j^*(\beta_L)\circ\alpha_{JL}\circ G_U(\eta_L)=\eta_{G_UL}.$$
The structure $J(\theta)\beta_L$ defines a functor on Weil pairs, and the specified open unit $\eta_{(L,\theta)}:(L,\theta)\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*J(L,\theta)$ is a Weil isomorphism with carrier exactly $\eta_L$. The comparisons, inverse units and this equation commute with rationalization and the specified common finite-field scalar extension maps; they are not arbitrary lifts of finite-reduction equalities.

If $\bar x:s=\operatorname{Spec}k\to X$ is a geometric point disjoint from $U$, the derived stalk vanishes:
$$L\bar x^*JL=0\quad\text{in }D^b_c(s,\Lambda),$$
naturally in $L\in D^b_c(U,\Lambda)$. More precisely, its integral counterpart vanishes for every $K\in D^b_c(U,\mathcal O_E)$ under the completed base-change comparison for the empty pullback open, transported to the actual integral pullback. This vanishing survives rationalization and common-stage passage. In the coefficient stalk convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], every stalk cohomology group outside $U$ is therefore zero.

proof.text: Work first over $R=\mathcal O_E$. The integral realization in [lem-zl-open-extension-texact-coefficient-stages] identifies the specified $J_R=R\lim_n\operatorname{Res}_n j_!K_n$ naturally with ordinary localized ringed-site $j_!K$, including its actual adjunction maps and specified coefficient comparisons. It also supplies Noetherianity of $X$ and quasi-compactness of $j$. By [lem-sf-open-roos-unit-adjunction], extension and restriction preserve completeness and the restricted open adjunction has section-normalized invertible unit $\eta_K:K\to j^*J_RK$. We use this identification throughout; no replacement by an arbitrarily chosen isomorphic operation is made.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-frobenius-open-square] with exponent $1$ to $j_0$; the Cartesian square has horizontal maps $g_U,g_X$ and vertical maps $j,j$. These are scheme automorphisms, not assumed $k$-linear. The equivalences and canonical comparison $\alpha:G_Uj^*\simeq j^*G_X$ are supplied by [lem-sf-automorphism-constructible-stage-equivalence]. In particular its actual ordinary-to-completed pullback comparisons are invertible on the integral objects at both endpoints. Apply [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] with adic datum $(R,(\varpi_E))$ to obtain the canonical $\beta:G_XJ_R\simeq J_RG_U$, transported by precisely those comparisons and Step 1. The DVR quotients and completeness hypotheses for this application are supplied by [lem-sf-open-roos-unit-adjunction].

proof.text:
Use [lem-sf-open-exchange-roos-restriction] for this same square. It identifies the completed exchange as $\lambda_j^{-1}R\lim(b_\bullet)$ and proves that its restriction is the pullback-composition identification after the open units. It also identifies the restricted ordinary-to-completed augmentation with the corresponding augmentation after composition. Consequently, under the actual comparisons of Steps 1 and 2, its displayed restriction equality is exactly
$$j^*(\beta_K)\circ\alpha_{J_RK}\circ G_U(\eta_K)=\eta_{G_UK}.$$
This conclusion uses the equality of strict Roos maps, including the completion units, asserted by the cited statement. It does not infer equality of integral maps from equality of their separate reductions.

proof.text: The comparisons of Step 1, the pullback compositors of Step 2, and the exchange and adjunction maps satisfy the coefficient squares of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]: these preserve the units and counits constructing exchange, and commute with rationalization and common-stage scalar extension. Thus the squares concern the specified compact-support coefficient action, as retained in [lem-zl-open-extension-texact-coefficient-stages], rather than a new choice of scalar maps. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-rational-transport] to localize the integral functors and transformations; the equation in Step 3 localizes since localization preserves composition. At $\Qlb$, represent the objects and arrows at a common finite coefficient field, apply that equation there, and use the same coefficient squares to pass to a larger field. Equality therefore holds in the common-stage category. Inverting the unit squares also proves the asserted compatibility of inverse units. This constructs $\beta$ and the normalized equation at both requested coefficients.

proof.text:
For a pair $(L,\theta)$ set $\theta_J=J(\theta)\circ\beta_L$. It is invertible. For a Weil arrow $u$, naturality of $\beta$ and $u\theta=\theta'G_U(u)$ give $J(u)\theta_J=\theta'_JG_X(J(u))$; identities and composition are preserved by $J$. Restriction has structure $j^*(\theta_J)\circ\alpha_{JL}$. Using Step 3 as transported in Step 4 and then naturality of the open unit gives
$$j^*J(\theta)\circ j^*(\beta_L)\circ\alpha_{JL}\circ G_U(\eta_L)
=j^*J(\theta)\circ\eta_{G_UL}=\eta_L\circ\theta.$$
This is exactly the Weil-arrow equation of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Hence the specified carrier $\eta_L$ is a Weil morphism. Its inverse is also a Weil morphism: multiply this equality by $\eta_L^{-1}$ on the left and $G_U(\eta_L^{-1})$ on the right. This proves the asserted Weil isomorphism with that exact carrier.

source.place: Part 2 extension-by-zero sentence: explicit calculation of the Weil unit from the normalized equation

proof.text:
Let $\bar x:s\to X$ be disjoint from $U$. Its pullback open $U\times_Xs$ is empty: its image in $s$ is precisely $\bar x^{-1}(U)$, the empty open. Apply [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison] to this square and the complete integral $K$, using Step 1 and its quasi-compactness of $j$. It gives
$$L\bar x^*_{\rm comp}J_RK\simeq j_{\varnothing!}L(\varnothing\to U)^*_{\rm comp}K=0.$$
Indeed, the pro-etale site of the empty scheme has only empty schemes as objects; its empty covering forces every module sheaf to be zero. Its complexes are therefore zero, and extension of the zero complex is zero. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], the actual integral pullback is exactly the specified strict reduction-limit construction, so the comparison just used gives vanishing for that operation itself. All arrows are natural in $K$; the resulting identification with zero is unique. This does not require $\bar x$ to be an immersion or ordinary pullback to preserve completeness.

proof.text: Localize the natural zero isomorphism of Step 6 at $E$, and then represent an object at $\Qlb$ at a finite coefficient stage. The pullback and compact-support coefficient compatibilities of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] identify these with the requested actual stalks, independently of enlarging the coefficient field. The zero comparison commutes with every scalar square because there is a unique map between zero objects. Finally [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] interprets a coefficient stalk cohomology group as $\mathrm H^a(\operatorname{Fib}_s(L\bar x^*JL))$. The formula of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] applies sections and rational tensor termwise, and at $\Qlb$ uses these same functors stagewise; it sends the zero complex to the zero complex. Thus every such group is $\mathrm H^a(0)=0$.

lean.statement:
theorem openWeilUnitAndEmptyFibre :
    ∃ (I : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E],
        IntegralData D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ E)
      (R : ∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E],
        RationalData D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ E),
      (∀ (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E],
        IntegralUnitNormalization D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ E (I E) ∧
          Rationalization D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ E (I E) (R E) ∧ WeilUnit (R E)) ∧
      ∀ S : Action D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ Ω,
        ∃ Q : CommonData D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ Ω S,
          WeilUnit Q ∧ FiniteScalarCompatibility D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ Ω S I R ∧
            CommonStageCompatibility D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ Ω S R Q ∧
            EmptyFibre D l hl X₀ U₀ j₀ Ω S R Q

statement_change.what: Remove the unnecessary separated-structure-morphism hypotheses, consistently with the arbitrary-scheme open-immersion and quasi-compact open-extension results in Stacks 09BN and 09BP. Finite type and quasi-compactness still supply Noetherianity; only the open map itself must be separated. The final section had unnecessarily restricted the algebraically closed coefficient universe to the scheme universe, although the underlying Action and coefficient-stage constructions already support independent universes; generalize that final section variable without changing any operation or normalization. To express the same vanishing with an independent closure universe, replace the restricted point-Qbar cohomology predicate by its literal finite-stage point cohomology. The preceding unchanged common-stage zero-object clause implies both; scalar extension of fields commutes with cohomology and is faithful. Replace the restricted localQbarPullbackStageIso uses by its identical eqToIso construction on finite inclusions.
